rv.q: In general, "Lucy and Leroy" strikes me a show needing a lot more development.
“Leroy and Lucy” is a smart and eventually provocative work, but inconsistently involving.
Ultimately, LEROY AND LUCY feels more like a sketch than a fully formed play.
Ultimately, Leroy and Lucy is a transcendent theatrical experience that bridges worlds—both cultural and spiritual.
Ngozi Anyanwu’s brilliant 90-minute, one-act play with music is absolutely mesmerizing and thoroughly entertaining.
This captivating production will leave you spellbound and is a must-see!

Playwright Ngozi Anyanwu is astutely aware of this in her entrancing world-premiere play “Leroy and Lucy” for Steppenwolf Theatre , which finds inspiration from the influential blues musician and songwriter Robert Johnson (1911-1938).
Epilogue aside, this is a moving and magical show, exploring the idea of human genius and transcendence.

Director Awoye Timpo keeps the text crisp, guiding Hill and Bradford through witty banter with expert timing, eliciting rolling waves of rich belly laughs. As things progress, it quickly becomes clear that Lucy is no ordinary woman, and that Leroy is flirting with more than just romance.A goddess perhaps?
Leroy and Lucy is a must-see production that showcases Steppenwolf’s commitment to storytelling that resonates nationally and internationally.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this atmospheric reimagining of the Robert Johnson legend through Yoruba mythology. Strong performances and haunting visuals earn praise, but some find the two-character piece dramatically inert.
